notes.subject: ir
notes.why_in_news: India and UAE held a joint committee meeting to review the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) and discuss expanding trade beyond oil and precious metals.
notes.fact_box: Bilateral trade between India and UAE exceeded $100 billion in 2024-25, marking a 19.6% growth over 2023-24. The nations have set a target to reach $100 billion in non-oil and non-precious metal trade by 2030.

prelims_pointers.text: CEPA: A Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement between India and the UAE.
Bilateral trade volume: Crossed $100 billion in the 2024-25 period.
Trade Target: $100 billion for non-oil and non-precious metal trade by 2030.
APEDA: Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority, involved in food safety MoUs.
Gold TRQ: India now allocates gold Tariff Rate Quotas through a transparent competitive bidding process.

notes.mains_question: Examine how Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreements (CEPAs) can serve as catalysts for diversifying India's trade basket beyond traditional commodities.
mains_dimensions: Trade diversification: Shifting focus from oil/precious metals to high-value services and processed food exports.
Regulatory alignment: Harmonizing food safety standards and pharmaceutical regulations to reduce non-tariff barriers.
Transparency in quotas: Utilizing competitive bidding for gold TRQs to ensure market integrity and fiscal discipline.
